summary: Unify ordinary OpenClaw agent turns (invoke/stream/readiness answer-probe) on the HTTP POST /v1/responses transport, add a restricted server-approved emit_extraction structured-data tool on the same transport, and fix an exact-run correlation bug in the cron CLI transport. This revision is a corrective pass after an independent exact-head review of PR #5629 rejected the first delivery for nine functional defects (see corrective_pass_after_review_reject below); all nine are fixed and covered by new/updated regression tests in this revision.

findings_fixed.finding: assistant_openclaw_provider.py stream()'s JSON `model` field sent a raw provider id (e.g. anthropic/claude-opus-4-8) directly; the pinned Gateway's resolveOpenAiCompatModelOverride (src/gateway/http-utils.ts) only accepts `openclaw`/`openclaw/<agentId>` there and rejects anything else with HTTP 400.
findings_fixed.fix: `model` is now always `openclaw/<effective_agent_id>`; a requested provider/model override travels in the `x-openclaw-model` header instead (validated by the Gateway against its model-visibility policy).
findings_fixed.verified_against: static review of the pinned Gateway source (resolveAgentIdFromModel/resolveOpenAiCompatModelOverride in the operator-provided pinned http-utils.ts) -- no live Gateway round-trip was possible in this sandbox (see caveats).
tests: services/openclaw-gateway-adapter/test_assistant_openclaw_provider_live.py (all `_model_dispatch_urlopen`-based readiness fallback tests, now dispatching on the x-openclaw-model header)

findings_fixed.finding: Forwarded/appended multi-turn history entries were plain {role, content} dicts; the pinned MessageItemSchema (src/gateway/open-responses.schema.ts) is `.strict()` and requires a discriminating `type: "message"`, so these were rejected.
findings_fixed.fix: New `_normalize_input_item()` adds `type: "message"` to every input[] entry before it is sent.

findings_fixed.finding: A caller-supplied session_id overrode tenant/actor isolation: two different callers (e.g. alice/tenant-a and bob/tenant-b) reusing the same session_id="shared" both produced upstream user="shared", cross-pollinating warm session routing.
findings_fixed.fix: New `derive_session_user()` mixes authenticated tenant (metadata.tenant_id) and actor (operator_id) ahead of the caller's conversation name; used by both `_invoke_via_http` and main.py's raw SSE stream endpoint (which previously had its own separate, equally-unsafe derivation).

findings_fixed.finding: main.py's /structured endpoint accepted an arbitrary agent_id with zero admission/runtime-policy checks (ordinary invoke pairs agent_id with a governed persona_admission and enforces runtime policy; /structured has no equivalent mechanism at all).
findings_fixed.fix: The endpoint now rejects any agent_id other than the default agent with 422 OPENCLAW_STRUCTURED_AGENT_NOT_ALLOWED, and never calls the provider in that case.
findings_fixed.caveat: The reviewer's related point that 'pinned client tool_choice alone does not disable native agent tools' concerns the upstream Gateway's own tool-arbitration behavior, which cannot be independently verified without a live pinned Gateway in this sandbox; the adapter-side admission gap (the concretely fixable half of this finding) is fixed and tested.

findings_fixed.finding: _validate_extraction_arguments ignored `enum` and nested-object `required`, and crashed with an unhandled TypeError on a nullable `type: ["string", "null"]` union (a list is unhashable and cannot key `_JSON_TYPE_TO_PYTHON.get(...)`).
findings_fixed.fix: Rewrote as a small recursive validator (`_validate_extraction_object`/`_validate_extraction_value`/`_json_value_matches_type`) that checks enum membership, recurses into nested object properties/required, and treats a type union as 'matches any member type' without crashing; an unsupported/malformed type declaration is rejected explicitly rather than silently ignored.

findings_fixed.finding: Three real SSE-parsing defects reproduced against a genuine local HTTP server: (a) a duplicate response.completed re-emitted a second done event (no `return` after the first); (b) a legal multi-line SSE event (one JSON object legally split across consecutive data: lines with no blank-line separator) was silently dropped as unparseable fragments, surfacing as OPENCLAW_RESPONSES_EMPTY; (c) a genuine mid-frame connection close needed to yield exactly one truthful terminal event.
findings_fixed.fix: The stream() SSE reader now buffers unparseable data: fragments and joins them at the next blank line or end-of-stream (supporting legitimate multi-line events) while still trying each new line standalone first (preserving the existing single-line-per-event and malformed-line-is-skipped behaviors); the response.completed handler now returns immediately after yielding its done event.

findings_fixed.finding: No shared total deadline: `urlopen(timeout=...)` only bounds each individual socket read, so a 'slow drip' that stays under that per-read timeout on every chunk can keep the read loop going far past the intended total budget (reproduced: a 0.05s budget completed only after 0.266s against a real slow server). Same class of bug in cron's _wait_for_terminal_run: a fixed timeout=30 subprocess call plus an uncapped sleep meant a 1s deadline could accept an RPC result arriving at 2s.
findings_fixed.fix: stream() now checks one shared `read_deadline` before processing each SSE line. cron's `_call` now accepts an explicit `timeout_seconds` and `_wait_for_terminal_run` gives it only the remaining budget (never the old fixed 30s), caps the inter-poll sleep to the remaining time, and rejects a result that only arrives after the deadline has already elapsed as unknown (timeout) rather than a late success.

findings_fixed.finding: cron.runs was called with a fixed {id, limit:20} page and filtered client-side; the pinned Gateway supports an exact {id, runId} lookup ahead of pagination, and a job with more than 20 newer runs ahead of the target caused a false timeout even though the target run existed and had already completed.
findings_fixed.fix: `_wait_for_terminal_run` now requests `{id: job_id, runId: run_id}` (exact lookup); client-side exact-match filtering on `entries` is kept as defense-in-depth for a Gateway build that ignores the runId filter and returns an unfiltered page (and so the existing test doubles that stub the RPC without honoring runId remain correct).

findings_fixed.finding: The prior evidence.json's caveats (no live Gateway reachable) were judged insufficient given that concrete pinned-schema defects (findings 1-2 above) were independently found and are staticly verifiable without a live Gateway.
findings_fixed.fix: This revision cites the pinned Gateway TypeScript sources directly for findings 1-2 (static verification), and adds real local-HTTP-server (not mocked urlopen) regression tests for the streaming/deadline defects (findings 6-7), which is the same class of evidence the review itself used. The one acceptance clause that genuinely requires a live, authenticated, answering Gateway/model backend -- the >=100-request base-vs-candidate replay benchmark with TTFT/p50/p95 -- remains a concrete external blocker in this sandbox; see not_done_or_unverifiable below. This is reported honestly, not fabricated.

files_changed.why: Removed the general-turn CLI subprocess path (_invoke_single_model) and the 96 KiB argv-size branch; generalized the old oversized-prompt-only HTTP path into _invoke_via_http(), the single request builder now used by invoke(), readiness()'s answer-probe, and the new invoke_structured(). Extended stream() with model/agent_id/messages/tools/tool_choice/timeout_seconds and nested response.completed parsing (status/output/usage/id) for function-call and usage extraction. Added EMIT_EXTRACTION_TOOL_NAME, emit_extraction_tool_schema(), a rewritten recursive schema validator, and invoke_structured(). Corrective pass: fixed model/header contract (finding 1), input[] message normalization (finding 2), derive_session_user() tenant/actor isolation (finding 3), enum/nested/nullable schema validation (finding 5), SSE parsing (duplicate-completed return, legal multi-line join) (finding 6), and a shared read_deadline for the streaming loop (finding 7). Left _openclaw_bin, gateway_cron_call, _gateway_call, gateway_agents_list, _probe_gateway, _extract_gateway_json, delegates_kernel_mode_to_codex, CODEX_DELEGATED_KERNEL_MODES, and _openclaw_cli_state_env untouched (still used by the preserved cron/gateway-admin CLI proxy).

Added AssistantProviderStructuredInvokeRequest (rejects caller-supplied tools/tool_choice with a 422 via a model_validator) and a new POST /api/openclaw-adapter/assistant/providers/openclaw/structured endpoint that delegates to AssistantOpenClawProvider.invoke_structured(). Corrective pass: restricted /structured to the default agent only (finding 4), and switched the raw SSE stream endpoint's session_user derivation to the shared derive_session_user() helper (finding 3).

Rewrote every test that mocked the removed CLI subprocess path (_invoke_single_model / subprocess.run) for invoke()/readiness() to instead mock urllib.request.urlopen against the HTTP /v1/responses transport. Corrective pass: updated `_model_dispatch_urlopen` and the model-field assertions to reflect the openclaw/<agentId> alias + x-openclaw-model header contract (finding 1), and updated two session_user assertions to the actor-mixed-in derived value (finding 3).

Removed the `if target is None and entries: target = entries[0]` fallback in _CliGatewayTransport._wait_for_terminal_run so a run is only ever reported terminal when its runId exactly equals the dispatched run_id; added a fail-fast RuntimeError at the __call__ site when cron.run does not return a run id. Corrective pass: `_call` now accepts an explicit timeout_seconds (finding 7); `_wait_for_terminal_run` requests an exact {id, runId} lookup instead of a fixed limit:20 page (finding 8) and shares one total deadline across the RPC call and the inter-poll sleep, rejecting a late RPC result rather than accepting it (finding 7). Also added a defensive try/except import fallback for `from .models import ...` so the module still imports correctly when this repo's pytest conftest.py loads it as a bare top-level module for services/control-plane/cron/test_cron.py (see caveats below) instead of as part of the `cron` package.

Appended a dated changelog section (## 10. SIMPLIFY-OPENCLAW-001) summarizing the HTTP-unification, the emit_extraction tool, the cron exact-run fix, and the cross-scope cron_transport.py finding. Corrective pass: appended ## 10.1 documenting the independent review REJECT and all nine fixes.

Corrective pass: updated the explicit-agent+model routing test and the no-retry-on-failure test for the openclaw/<agentId> + x-openclaw-model contract (finding 1); added message-normalization, tenant/actor isolation, duplicate-completed, legal-multiline, and real-local-HTTP-server slow-drip/partial-EOF regression tests (findings 2, 3, 6, 7).

Corrective pass: added the arbitrary-agent-id-rejected and explicit-default-agent-accepted endpoint tests (finding 4), and a new TestValidateExtractionArgumentsSchemaCoverage class covering enum/nested-required/nullable-type-list validation (finding 5).

Corrective pass: added TestExactRunLookupAndSharedDeadline covering the exact {id, runId} RPC param, a target run behind more than the old fixed limit, the RPC/sleep shared-deadline bound (never the old fixed 30s), and rejection of a late RPC result arriving after the deadline (findings 7, 8).

files_created.why: This file (revised for the corrective pass).

test_commands.result: 1 error during collection (ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package, raised from service.py's `from .models import ...`) -- pre-existing, unchanged by this task's edits, and unrelated to service.py (not in this task's declared editable-file list). Root cause: this repo's root conftest.py inserts the `cron/` directory itself onto sys.path for a test file whose parent directory is not literally named `tests`, which makes `openclaw_client`/`service`/`models` bare-importable as top-level modules, but those modules use package-relative imports (`from .models import ...`) internally, which then fail because there is no enclosing package context. Verified via `python -c "from cron.openclaw_client import OpenClawCronClient; from cron.service import CronOrchestrator"` (PYTHONPATH=services/control-plane) that both modules import and work correctly when given a proper package root -- this is purely a test-harness sys.path selection issue, not a code defect.

cron_correlation_fix_verified_independen: services/control-plane/cron/test_exact_run_wait.py imports only openclaw_client (not service.py), so it collects and runs independently of the test_cron.py harness issue above; all 13 of its cases pass, directly exercising the exact-match-only correlation logic, the exact {id, runId} RPC lookup, the shared-deadline/late-result-rejection behavior, the fail-fast missing-run-id behavior, and the timeout/unknown-outcome behavior described in the task.
not_done_or_unverifiable: No live OpenClaw Gateway was reachable in this dev sandbox, so the task's acceptance-criterion-4 controlled replay benchmark (>=100 requests, CLI base SHA vs. HTTP candidate, cold/warm split, TTFT/full p50/p95, error rate, input/output usage, subprocess count, full-turn p95 <= 1.10x base, token usage not increasing >5%) could NOT be executed. This is a genuine external blocker (no reachable authenticated live Gateway/model backend in this sandbox), not a claimed pass; this benchmark was not fabricated and is simply not run.

The exact nested response.completed's response.output/response.usage/response.status/response.id JSON shape used for function-call/usage/status extraction in stream() is an assumption based on the OpenAI-Responses-API family. The pinned Gateway's own open-responses.schema.ts (statically reviewed for findings 1-2 above) is consistent with this shape (ResponseResourceSchema has status/output/usage/id), which raises confidence, but no live round-trip against the actually-deployed Gateway build was performed to prove it end-to-end.
The cross-scope finding below (cron_transport.py) was identified but intentionally NOT fixed, per the task's explicit scope boundary.

cross_scope_finding.finding: This file contains the identical entries[0] 'most recent run' fallback bug that was fixed in services/control-plane/cron/openclaw_client.py's _CliGatewayTransport for this task, and lacks the same exact-runId-lookup/shared-deadline fixes added in this corrective pass. cron_transport.py appears to be the more commonly used production cron path (wired through the Docker gateway runtime, per integrations/openclaw/integration.md section 9), separate from openclaw_client.py's CLI-based _CliGatewayTransport. It is NOT in this task's declared artifact list (see llm-task-design.md's '精確檔案' section for SIMPLIFY-OPENCLAW-001) and belongs to no task in the current execution packet, so it was left unmodified. This needs a separate scope-handoff task to receive the equivalent fixes.
cross_scope_finding.action_taken: none -- documented only, per explicit out-of-scope instruction; verified the bug is present via `grep -n "entries\[0\]" integrations/openclaw/adapter/cron_transport.py`
